newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul hopes Pyongyang will attend IPU meeting.
newsitem.headline: Seoul hopes Pyongyang will attend IPU meeting.

text.p: South Korea said on Tuesday it wanted North Korean parliamentary members to participate in a global conference for lawmakers to be held in Seoul in April.
"North Korea was invited through its Geneva mission late last December," Kang Jang-seok, director general for South Korea's Inter-Parliament Bureau, told reporters.
"We hope that North Korea will attend the conference. But we have had no response yet."
The Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) will open its 97th conference in Seoul on April 10-15 to discuss international cooperation for global and regional security and stability.
The topic was chosen in view of current problems on the Korean peninsula, Kang said.

The defection of Pyongyang's top ideologue Hwang Jang-yop, who arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday after seeking asylum at Seoul's Beijing mission in mid-February, has posed the latest strain on fragile inter-Korean relations.
Hwang ranked 24th in North Korea's hierarchy.
North and South Korea remain technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce not a peace agreement.

Hosts of the IPU are obliged to invite all 135 member nations to the biannual meeting, Kang said. Some 1,000 participants from over 100 countries were expected at the Seoul conference, South Korean officials said.

South Korean representatives visited Pyongyang in 1991 to attend an IPU conference there. Seoul hosted the IPU meeting once before in 1983. The first IPU conference kicked off in Paris in 1889 for world peace and cooperation.
